newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev rises, c.bank seen halting advance.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev rises, c.bank seen halting advance.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,475-1,485 per dollar, up from the opening's 1,500-1,510 and 1,520-1,525 at the previous close as the central bank was seen containing the lev rise, dealers said.
"The central bank started bidding for cheap dollars in the afternoon and halted the lev advance near 1,480," a commercial bank dealer said. Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Local currency gained around 45 levs to the dollar on the day on ample dollar supply from domestic and foreign investors eyeing high-yield local debt, traders said.
Foreign investors, attracted by high yields and pending privatisation sell-offs, have stepped up byuing Bulgarian government securities with maturity over six months.
Dollar-denominated bad-debt bonds, or ZUNKs have attracted foreign investors interest because they are accepted as means of payment at par value in the privatisation of Bulgarian state firms.
"ZUNKs now trade near their minimum acceptable price of 45 percent which makes them an attractive investment," a Post Bank dealer said.
In 1994 Bulgaria issued 32 billion levs of lev-denominated bad debt bonds and $1.8 billion of dollar-denominated ZUNKs to cover unperforming loans extended to state companies before 1991.
Some 20 billion lev worth of lev-denominated ZUNKs and around $940 million of dollar-denominated ones were in circulation at end-March, central bank figures showed.
Lev-denominated ZUNKs also can be used as means of payment at par in sell-offs. Their minimum acceptable price is now set at 35 percent of par. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
